features.source_rule: Table 265: BBox is normalized lower-left then upper-right in measuring coordinates; its ordering sets positive-axis orientation independently of page rotation and is independent of O. Name is a descriptive UI string. Measure specifies scale/units for contents in viewport. PtData is optional PDF 2.0 extended geospatial data.
features.consumer: pdf_model::measurement::Viewport/Viewports; viewer_core Query::Measure consumes page viewports. Image-XObject Measure query gap is separately captured by B73 and is not repeated here.
features.assertions: Model tests cover viewport containment, array reverse-order selection, and first-point selection. Public measuring tests assert viewport names and paths; numeric distinct-scale first-point control is in measurement_geospatial_current / T52 and must not be counted as new here. The source's bbox-axis orientation and O independence are not proved by a name-only assertion; model implementation reads signs/origin separately. No additional failure is asserted in this shard.
features.status: bounded coverage; no new defect asserted

features.source_rule: Table 266: Type optional with Measure value; Subtype optional with RL or PDF 2.0 GEO; other subtypes may be used; default RL.
features.consumer: pdf_model::measurement::measure_dictionary; viewer Query and annotation measurement consumers use the parsed subtype.
features.assertions: a_geospatial_measure_carries_the_earth_model_and_not_a_scale exercises GEO; rectilinear fixtures exercise RL. Not a comprehensive acceptance/rejection test of every unknown subtype, which the source explicitly permits.
features.status: bounded model behavior covered; no unknown-subtype mandate inferred

features.source_rule: Table 267: R/X/D/A required; Y required only when axis units or factors differ; T and S optional; O defaults to BBox lower-left; CYX only meaningful with Y, and without CYX distance/area/angle may not be performed. Axis factors are applied before distance/area; slope does not require CYX.
features.consumer: Rectilinear model converts axes before distance/area, honors viewport orientation and O, and exposes distance/area/angle/slope through Query::Measure.
features.assertions: a_distance_is_measured_in_the_first_points_viewport_with_its_axes_scaled_first has literal unequal X/Y/CYX value and a 1:1 control; two_axes_with_no_conversion_between_them_have_no_distance checks absence; slope and angle model tests have literal values. Public query's standard worked-example path currently checks the result's unit fragments and absent slope, not its exact length/area string; its model-level standard example is exact. No broader crosswalk of every optional-field combination is claimed.
features.status: core numeric behavior has independent literals; public end-to-end formatting assertion is weaker than the model oracle

features.source_rule: Each array contains one or more NumberFormat dictionaries in descending granularity. Table 268 defines required U/C; F defaults D and applies only to the last dictionary; D defaults to 100 for decimal and 16 for fractional display; FD controls retaining low-order decimal zeros / unreduced denominator; RT and RD default comma/period; SS/PS default one space; O defaults suffix placement. §12.9.2 carries fractional remainders through the array and the example's literal result is 1 mi 2,378 ft 7 5/8 in. FD=false permits reducing fractions/truncating zeros, rather than requiring that presentation. Trimming final spacing is also a documented implementation choice.
features.consumer: number_format parses the Table 268 values; measurement::format implements the algorithm; Query::Measure returns formatted strings to hosts.
features.assertions: the_clauses_own_example_formats_the_string_it_states compares exact standard output, including grouping and fractional eighths. each_value_of_f_shows_the_fraction_its_own_way directly tests F= D/F/R/T, D=100/16, FD true/false with exact values. a_value_with_no_fraction_stops_at_the_first_unit tests O=P and the default spacing. The public query test reaches the standard dictionary but only checks starts_with/contains/ends_with, not the numeric result; the model exact test does not traverse PDF dictionary parsing and the public API together. Explicit custom RD/RT and parser-level FD/default combinations lack a single public end-to-end literal witness in the inspected tests.
features.status: model algorithm is strongly tested; narrow public parser-to-query assertion gap drafted for decimal precision/separator and default control
